pos.personaBrief: Counter-attacking system built from midfield backwards with up to seven defensive roles, criticised as too defensive; Maradona touches and Burruchaga supply in transition.

pro.personaBrief: Counter-attack with Valdano's clipped balls over the line and quick break chances; Batista a safe ball-winner in front of the back three.

est.personaBrief: Defined roles (sweeper, markers, wing-backs, Batista) but Maradona roams free as nominal second striker and wing-backs hold width.

lar.personaBrief: 3-5-2 without wingers; width only from wing-backs Giusti and Olarticoechea, with a crowded central midfield giving Maradona room.

blo.personaBrief: Compact, midfield-heavy defence with sweeper behind markers and a counter-attacking approach; no pressing evidence, so waiting rather than pressing.

mar.personaBrief: Ruggeri and Cuciuffo man-marked centre-forwards (Galderisi, Francescoli); plan for Matthaus on Maradona; Bilardo's corner-focused preparation.

pla.personaBrief: Bilardo changed shape and personnel by opponent (Cuciuffo for Galderisi, extra midfielder against England, dropping Pasculli), preparing around rivals.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic anti-futbol; 'second is a failure'; team criticised for being too defensive; results first.

sis.personaBrief: A drilled defensive platform (3-5-2 practised two years) gave Maradona total freedom; unknown defenders made to work.

jog.personaBrief: Maradona as classic creator protected by robust ball-winners (Batista) and marking stoppers; physical and aerial duels valued.

bas.personaBrief: Squad of seasoned internationals around Maradona, with no youth emphasis; Bilardo picked solid experienced players.

lid.personaBrief: Bilardo the authoritarian boss who axed captain Passarella and made Maradona captain; he decides line-ups and shows no sign of consulting.
